question: What can infant adverse-event reports involving acetaminophen tell a researcher, and what can they not establish about how often side effects occur or whether the medicine caused them? Use the MCP and state the age scope actually queried.
criteria: Report only retrieved counts/events and exact cohort age scope. Reports not incidence or causation; cannot generalize a subset to all infants. Cite returned query. If retrieval fails, disclose it rather than invent counts.
answer:
**Age scope queried:** acetaminophen FAERS reports for patients aged **0 through 12 months**, where age was coded in months. Other age-unit encodings were excluded. This is not all infants. [S1](https://api.fda.gov/drug/event.json?search=patient.drug.openfda.generic_name%3A%22acetaminophen%22+AND+patient.patientonsetageunit%3A802+AND+patient.patientonsetage%3A%5B0+TO+12%5D&count=patient.reaction.reactionmeddrapt.exact&limit=25)

### What these reports can tell a researcher

They show the **volume and types of reports submitted** in this queried infant-filtered dataset. Examples included vomiting (117 reports), pyrexia (98), rash (60), irritability (42), seizure (35), and liver injury (28). The query also returned product-use and administration-related terms. These are reported reaction terms, not necessarily confirmed adverse effects. [S1](https://api.fda.gov/drug/event.json?search=patient.drug.openfda.generic_name%3A%22acetaminophen%22+AND+patient.patientonsetageunit%3A802+AND+patient.patientonsetage%3A%5B0+TO+12%5D&count=patient.reaction.reactionmeddrapt.exact&limit=25)

They can therefore help identify reporting patterns and generate questions for further investigation. In this MCP lookup, the source population for each reaction was **not established** beyond the query’s age filter, and applicability to a confirmed age band was not confirmed in the reaction-level metadata. [S1](https://api.fda.gov/drug/event.json?search=patient.drug.openfda.generic_name%3A%22acetaminophen%22+AND+patient.patientonsetageunit%3A802+AND+patient.patientonsetage%3A%5B0+TO+12%5D&count=patient.reaction.reactionmeddrapt.exact&limit=25)

### What they cannot establish

- **How often side effects occur:** FAERS counts are reporting volume, not incidence or risk. The query has no exposure denominator, so these counts cannot estimate the frequency of side effects or individual risk. [S1](https://api.fda.gov/drug/event.json?search=patient.drug.openfda.generic_name%3A%22acetaminophen%22+AND+patient.patientonsetageunit%3A802+AND+patient.patientonsetage%3A%5B0+TO+12%5D&count=patient.reaction.reactionmeddrapt.exact&limit=25)
- **Whether acetaminophen caused an event:** spontaneous reports do not establish causation. A reported event may have other explanations, including the underlying illness or other exposures, but this lookup did not establish those factors for the listed reports. [S1](https://api.fda.gov/drug/event.json?search=patient.drug.openfda.generic_name%3A%22acetaminophen%22+AND+patient.patientonsetageunit%3A802+AND+patient.patientonsetage%3A%5B0+TO+12%5D&count=patient.reaction.reactionmeddrapt.exact&limit=25)
- **Safety from absence of reports:** no report, or a low count, would not prove that an event cannot occur or that the medicine is safe.

The MCP’s interpretation is therefore limited to describing reported-event patterns; it is not clinical validation or a causal or incidence analysis. [S1](https://api.fda.gov/drug/event.json?search=patient.drug.openfda.generic_name%3A%22acetaminophen%22+AND+patient.patientonsetageunit%3A802+AND+patient.patientonsetage%3A%5B0+TO+12%5D&count=patient.reaction.reactionmeddrapt.exact&limit=25)[S2](https://open.fda.gov/apis/drug/event/)
